statement.p: Trinity is conducting market research on the cost of a cell phone data plan. Trinity has determined that the average annual cost of a cell phone data plan is 1297, and that the distribution of costs is normally distributed with a standard deviation of 86.
a. Find the probability that a single randomly selected consumer spends less than 1244 on a cell phone data plan.
b. The cost of the middle 40 of cell phone data plans falls between (round to the nearest dollar):
c. The most expensive 7 of cell phone data plans cost at least how much annually?

solution.p: Define the normal distribution in Desmos: \displaystyle\text{normaldist}{\left({1297},{86}\right)}.
a. In Desmos, select LEFT region, compute AREA. Enter the boundary 1244 and obtain the probability: \displaystyle{P}{\left({x}\leq{1244}\right)}={0.269}./p

b. For the middle 40 of the data, select INNER region, compute BOUNDS. Enter the area of the middle region \displaystyle{0.40} and obtain the upper and lower bounds: \displaystyle{1252}\leq{x}\leq{1342} .
Alternatively (old Desmos approach): split the remaining region between the tails and find the boundaries:

c. For the most expensive 7 of the distribution, need \displaystyle{0.07} of the area to the right. Use a RIGHT region, compute BOUNDS and enter the area to the right \displaystyle{0.07}. Obtain the lower bound: \displaystyle{x}={1424}.
